transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi. Yeah, thanks for seeing me. Um... so I guess what finally made me make this appointment is that I just keep forgetting basic adult things. Like paying bills, or returning emails for job interviews. Which is really stressful because I just graduated, and my friend Sarah actually got a job in marketing right out of school—even though she doesn't even like marketing! She wanted to do graphic design, but she took it because they get free catered lunches on Fridays. Which sounds amazing, honestly. I love a good sandwich spread. 

But um... wait, what was I saying? Right, my life. I just keep missing those emails, and I'm not showing up for appointments, or following through on basic errands. I went to the store yesterday just for paper towels and walked out with two houseplants and no paper towels. It's just... it's starting to cost me real opportunities, like actual jobs, and I feel like I'm messing everything up because I can't keep track of anything.
Did you have similar problems with attention, forgetfulness, or losing track of things when you were a child?

Yeah, oh my gosh, yes. It's always been like this. Like, even back in elementary school, my teachers were always writing on my report cards that I was, you know, "bright but distracted." I was constantly losing my worksheets. Like, they would just vanish. My desk was this absolute black hole of crumpled papers and broken crayons, and I could never find my homework when it was time to turn it in. 

And I was always talking out of turn, too. I remember in third grade, Mrs. Gable—she was this really strict lady who always wore these giant, colorful statement necklaces. Like, huge chunky beads. I used to stare at them while she was talking and wonder if they were heavy, or if she made them herself, because my aunt used to make jewelry like that and sell it at craft fairs. She made this one really pretty turquoise bracelet for me once, but I lost it at a water park... 

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, school. Yeah, I'd rush through all the directions on tests and just completely mess them up, or I'd blurt out answers without raising my hand. My desk was just so messy I could never find anything. So yeah, it's definitely been happening since I was a kid.
Do these attention and organization problems happen in more than one setting, like at work or school and also at home?

Yeah, pretty much everywhere. Like, my apartment right now is a total disaster zone. I have clean laundry sitting in a basket from, like, two weeks ago, and I just keep picking clothes out of it instead of putting them away. Which is so annoying because then everything gets wrinkled. I actually bought this handheld steamer to fix the wrinkles, because I saw this influencer using one on TikTok and it looked so satisfying. She was steaming this beautiful silk dress, and it just made me want to buy silk dresses, even though I have nowhere to wear them. I mean, I guess I could wear one to the grocery store, but that seems a little extra, right? 

Anyway, um... yeah, so home is a mess. And school was just as bad. I was always the person frantically finishing a paper in the library ten minutes before it was due, surrounded by energy drink cans. And even when I go to my parents' house, my mom is always getting on my case about leaving my stuff all over the kitchen counter. She has this pristine granite countertop, and she hates it when I leave my keys and mail there. She's really into interior design now, actually. She just repainted their living room this color called "Sea Salt" and it looks... wait. 

Sorry, I'm doing it again. But yeah, it's not just one place. It's home, school, my parents' house... basically anywhere I go, the chaos just kind of follows me.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety, like you have trouble sitting still?

Oh, definitely. It's like physical torture. Whenever I have to sit through an interview, or a long meeting, or even just trying to watch a movie, I get this intense pressure inside my body. Like I absolutely have to get up, or shift around in my seat, or do something with my hands, otherwise I feel like I'm literally going to crawl out of my skin. 

Actually, speaking of movies, I went to the theater last week with my roommate to see that new sci-fi one. Have you seen it? The soundtrack was incredible, but the seats in that theater were so weird. They were those fancy leather ones that recline, but the button on mine was jammed, so I was stuck halfway back the entire time. My roommate got a giant bucket of popcorn and spilled half of it because she got jump-scared by this loud explosion scene. I love popcorn, but only if it has an absurd amount of that fake movie theater butter on it. I tried making it at home once with nutritional yeast because a girl on Instagram said it tastes exactly like cheddar cheese, but it really doesn't. It just tastes like dusty vitamins. I bought a huge jar of it too, and now it's just sitting in my pantry next to a mini waffle maker I've never even plugged in. I bought it because it makes waffles shaped like dinosaurs, which is cute, but who has time to make dinosaur waffles on a Tuesday? 

But um... wait. What were you asking me? Oh, right, fidgeting. Yeah, sitting still is basically impossible for me. I always have to be messing with something or I just feel that awful pressure building up.
